contract.note: Testing recurring incremental revenue attributable to subsidies is fair. Examining unsuccessful launches avoids selection bias; the wording need not mean every launch inevitably produces a surge.

reviews.rationale: Neither source links VC-funded subsidies to incremental lab revenue around launches. Uneven uptake challenges automatic enthusiasm, while rapid share gains may reflect substitution. Neither settles the asserted mechanism.

contract.note: Requiring comparable-scale replacement of the identified capacity fairly tests the forecast. Unrelated purchases and abandoned expansion negotiations cannot resolve it.

evidence.note: The dated report distinguishes a never-finalized expansion from existing commitments. It predates the forecast and establishes no qualifying replacement event.

Crusoe's company disclosure identifies substantial Microsoft demand, but does not establish replacement purchases of the labs' identified commitments. Announced power capacity alone does not establish comparable economic scale.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated. The packet establishes neither comparable-scale replacement purchases of relinquished committed capacity nor its final irreversible disposition. Other large buyers provide countercontext but do not meet the early-resolution rule.

contract.note: Assessing contemporaneous expectations and material funding dependencies is fair. The Azure input's combined-versus-per-lab interpretation changes the stated subtotal from $174 billion to $224 billion; the contract appropriately leaves this unresolved.

evidence.note: Broadcom's filing discloses a commercial-success dependency for one expansion. It does not establish the three-provider revenue estimate or the asserted financing and customer-funding chain.

The timely report provides concentration context, including a prior-year customer example. It does not establish customer financing status, the 2027 revenue estimate or necessary dependence on new capital.

reviews.rationale: The original analyst estimates and a complete financing model are absent. Ambiguous Azure arithmetic cannot independently prove or disprove the threshold. Concentration reporting and one disclosed commercial dependency do not establish the full causal chain.
